# Interior contacts for a minimal empty cap family

Let N=n+d. Suppose k closed caps

`H_i={w:a_i.w>=b_i}`

have empty complementary intersection `intersection_i {a_i.w<=b_i}`.
Assume the family is minimal for covering S and has strict exclusive
witnesses: p_i in C is strictly in H_i and strictly outside every other cap.
(The p_i may initially be mixed-integer witnesses.)

## 1. The full-size refinement is valid

If k=N+1, minimal emptiness implies that the normals form a full-rank
positive circuit. Thus there are lambda_i>0 with

`sum lambda_i a_i=0`, `B=-sum lambda_i b_i>0`.

The positive circuit is minimal and has rank N. The original cap intersection

`T=intersection_i H_i`

is a nondegenerate bounded simplex. Introduce its barycentric coordinates

`L_i(w)=lambda_i(a_i.w-b_i)/B`, with `sum L_i=1`.

For each exclusive witness p_j, L_i(p_j)<0 when i!=j, while the column sum
is 1. The witness coordinate matrix is strictly column diagonally dominant
with positive diagonal and negative off-diagonal entries. Its inverse is
entrywise nonnegative by the Neumann-series argument recorded in
`candidate e711a2f2fa42ce54`. Hence T is contained in conv{p_i}.

Uniformly increase the complementary thresholds from b_i to b_i+delta. The
first feasible value is

`delta_0=B/(sum lambda_i)>0`.

The unique contact q satisfies `a_i.q=b_i+delta_0` for every i. All its
original cap margins equal delta_0>0, so q lies in int(T). Consequently

`q in int(T) subset int(conv{p_i}) subset int(C)`.

This proves the proposed interior-contact refinement WITHOUT needing any
additional general-position assumption when the family already has N+1
members.

If all caps have mass strictly below a fixed threshold, a sufficiently small
translation of q off the integer projection preserves those strict bounds,
provided the cap normals are nonvertical. A further sufficiently small
uniform threshold increase makes the complementary simplex a bounded
full-dimensional lattice-free body contained in int(C). The strict interior
location supplies the required geometric margin.

## 2. Smaller minimal empty families cannot generally be made generic while
## retaining emptiness

Take n=d=1, `C=[0,1] x [-1,1]`, and the two caps

`H_1={x>=-1/4}`, `H_2={x<=1/4}`.

Their open versions cover C (indeed the whole plane), and (0,1),(1,-1) are
strict exclusive mixed-integer witnesses. Their complementary intersection
`{x<=-1/4, x>=1/4}` is empty. Each cap has normalized mixed mass 5/8.

For every small eta>0, replace H_1 by

`H_1^eta={eta z+x>=-1/4}`,

leaving H_2 unchanged. The two normals are now linearly independent, and the
strict exclusive witnesses persist for eta<3/4. But their complementary
intersection is NONEMPTY:

`x>=1/4`, `z<=(-1/4-x)/eta`.

In general, any k<=N independent normals admit a solution to the equations
`a_i.w=b_i` and hence cannot form an empty closed-halfspace intersection.
Therefore a minimal empty family with k<N+1 cannot be perturbed into full
general position while retaining emptiness. Emptiness was stable in the
unconditional auxiliary-Q construction only because the larger, nonminimal
family retained positive spanning of all N ambient directions.

## 3. What remains true for a smaller family

For general k, the minimal positive circuit has rank k-1. Its cap intersection
is a simplex cylinder, and the first complementary intersection under uniform
relaxation is an affine flat. The barycentric-coordinate/M-matrix argument
still shows that this flat meets the convex hull of the exclusive witnesses.

One can additionally move each witness slightly into int(C), preserving all
strict cap signs (these moved witnesses need not remain mixed-integer).
Their convex combination representing the critical barycentric vector then
shows that the critical flat meets int(C).

This does NOT make the entire critical flat a singleton, bounded, or contained
in C. Additional caps needed to control its free directions require an
independent cap-mass argument. Thus the full-size interior-simplex refinement
cannot be applied to a smaller family merely by asserting genericity.
